finalists.label: Sickle Cell Retinopathy
finalists.why: It has the most specific and relevant evidence, including peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions and hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL.

finalists.label: Sickle Cell Maculopathy
finalists.why: It is a subtype of sickle cell retinopathy and has no evidence against it, but lacks specific evidence for it.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions and hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL, which are specific to sickle cell retinopathy, decided the final comparison.

support_spans: Hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL, corresponding to ophthalmoscopically opaque areas
A young black woman with sickle cell disease (HbSS variant) presented with a 2-day history of visual loss in the left eye
Visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/800 OS
abnormal retinal capillary bed across the macula, with increased intercapillary spacing and small areas of hypofluorescence nasal to the fovea
In her left eye, ischemic macular whitening was noted
contradict_spans: No cherry-red spot, hemorrhage, or peripheral neovascularization was present
